opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: The main applicant must have BES membership (not required for all working group members). Groups of 8-15 individuals with a diverse mix of career stages, institutions, genders, ethnicities and international participation; not formed entirely of academic institution members.
opportunities.summary: Funds the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 individuals to analyse and synthesise existing data using a hypothesis and question-led approach, fostering collaboration and mentoring.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for a decade of data collection; first five years' funding (£3,500) claimable in year 1, with an additional £3,500 claimable in year 6.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners (e.g. Reserve Managers, consultants) and university academics. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with at least 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies such as restoration, habitat creation, alien species control and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to life-long learning, formal or informal settings), including those in industry. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Projects max 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices in ecology to improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching, including evidence-based examples of innovative practice, systematic reviews, exploring emerging education research areas, and disseminating best practice.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants

amount.raw: Grant awards of up to £20,000 can be claimed.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations. Undergraduates and masters students are not eligible. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Placements can be full-time or part-time up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Funds an immersive secondment placement (up to 12 months) that places an ecologist in a distinctly different discipline or sector (e.g. another discipline, NGO/charity, public sector, business) to develop interdisciplinary skills and foster relationships between disciplines and sectors.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Member-only grant. Provides funding for researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Not a scholarship; does not cover principal researcher salary, bench fees or departmental vehicle hire. BES funding cannot be used towards completion of an undergraduate or master's degree or funded fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Supports new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus, advancing ecological science.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels to organise ecological public engagement events. Projects max 12 months. No restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Supports BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science, in diverse formats including in-person events, digital formats or physical resources.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £250 is available to cover registration fees for virtual conferences/courses; a maximum of £500 is available for events in person.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (registered on a postgraduate research degree programme). Postdocs, undergraduates and masters students are not eligible. Must work/study at a university or research institution and work in scientific areas within the BES remit.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to network and publicise their research by presenting at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending the meeting such as registration, transport, food and accommodation. Awarded via a lottery-based system.
